preamble: All across solutions and their letter counts are deficient in a consistent way.

clue.text: Done for, finished with, done with abandoned women

indicators.note: abandoned suggests letters let loose from their order, so the fodder is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has finished with a relationship and walked out on the women in their life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' turns DONE WITH plus W into the entry. As the preamble says, every across entry drops OUT OF, so the definition really defines OUT OF THE WINDOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrown out of the window is an idiom for something discarded or finished; the grid omits the opening two words.

clue.text: Thomas the Rhymer loves to bewitch

parts.note: Thomas Hood was an English poet, so a rhymer called Thomas; the surface invokes the Scottish seer Thomas the Rhymer
love is zero in tennis, written O, so two loves are OO

explanation.surface: The legendary Scottish prophet Thomas the Rhymer delights in casting spells.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas the Rhymer is a figure of Scottish legend, but here it means the Victorian poet Thomas Hood.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a jinx or spell on someone is a voodoo-derived verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Spheres of interest — example of limnologist's is wrapped up in mine!

indicators.note: wrapped up in says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: my words, read as what the speaker of the clue says: the words are mine
a limnologist studies lakes, so an example of one's subject is a lake, abbreviated L

explanation.surface: A scientist claims a fellow specialist's field of study is bound up with their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' is the setter's own WORDS, and a limnologist studies freshwater lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's worlds are the fields or areas of activity they move in, such as the world of sport.

clue.text: Fashionable backing drums, maybe, on a hit for Elton

indicators.note: backing means the word for fashionable is written from right to left

parts.note: in means fashionable
a drum kit is a set of drums, so drums are an example of a kit

explanation.surface: A trendy band's drummer plays on one of Elton John's hits.
explanation.definitionFit: Elton John had a 1985 hit single with this woman's name as its title.

clue.text: "XL" fly-by-night to whom "L" is made to fit

indicators.note: letters made to fit something are reworked into a new shape, here a new order

explanation.surface: An extra-large shirt for a dodgy character, whose size L must be altered to fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made to fit' rearranges TO WHOM plus L. XL means extra large, and a fly-by-night is a creature of the night.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical species is one of the largest moths, active after dark, hence a very big night flier.

clue.text: Horsey crowd I spotted in field?

indicators.note: spotted in says one piece has been seen inside another

parts.note: the field is all the runners in a race, the racers
ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: A horsey person spots someone in a crowded field.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectators at a horse race are a crowd of people interested in horses.

clue.text: Outside plant promoted item providing stable security

parts.note: hors is French for outside, as in hors d'oeuvre

indicators.note: promoted in a down entry means moved upwards, so the plant word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a liane is a climbing plant, a variant of liana

explanation.surface: An outdoor plant is given more prominence by a gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' is French here: hors. The stable is a horse's, and the item secures its shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail used to fix a shoe to a hoof keeps a stable animal's shoe secure.

clue.text: Row on street, punching a joker

indicators.note: punching means driving into the middle of another piece

parts.note: per means a, as in so much a head
a rank is a row, as of soldiers

explanation.surface: A row breaks out in the street and someone punches a comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical joker plays tricks on people, a synonym for one who pulls pranks.

clue.text: Eggs turned down at the edges not so popular now

indicators.note: down at the edges puts the down word round the outside of the eggs

parts.note: fur is soft fine hair, like down

indicators.note: turned means the word for eggs is flipped round

parts.note: ova is Latin for eggs

explanation.surface: Eggs that are turned down at the edges are no longer fashionable at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: As the preamble says, the definition defines the full phrase OUT OF FAVOUR, which loses its first two words in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer in favour has lost its popularity, the full idiom beginning with the dropped words.

clue.text: Sky broadcast with Lulu or Gaga?

indicators.note: broadcast literally means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Sky TV is showing either Lulu or Lady Gaga.
explanation.walkthrough: Lulu and Lady Gaga are singers, but 'gaga' also means crazy: OUT OF YOUR SKULL, losing its first two words in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being off your head or crazy is an idiom for mental confusion, and gaga means senile or mad.

clue.text: Scents include one backtracking when hunting is illegal

indicators.note: backtracking means the whole thing is read in the reverse direction
include means one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: to scent is to nose, so scents means noses
a means one

explanation.surface: Hounds pick up scents and backtrack during the closed part of the hunting year.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble removes OUT OF; the closed months for hunting are out of season.
explanation.definitionFit: Game may not be hunted during the closed period of the year, the idiom for which opens with the omitted words.

clue.text: Learn to suppress rumour one's unfit

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down within, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: to con is to learn or study
an on dit is a piece of gossip, from the French for they say
I is one, the Roman numeral; the 's is the link is

explanation.surface: Learning to keep a rumour quiet makes someone unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: ON DIT, French 'they say', is used in English for a rumour. The full phrase is OUT OF CONDITION.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has lost fitness through lack of exercise is said to be in poor shape, the idiom with the dropped words.

clue.text: Off limits — university patrolled by Moore and Craig?

indicators.note: a place patrolled by guards has them all around it, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: Roger Moore and Daniel Craig both played James Bond, so they are Bonds

explanation.surface: A university campus is guarded by two James Bond actors, so it is off limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbidden territory is described with this idiom, which opens with the dropped words.

clue.text: Roast weasel Spooner's provided for regatta marker

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the starts of words, so the opening sounds of the two pieces trade places

parts.note: to roast is to bake
a stoat is a member of the weasel family

explanation.surface: A roast weasel is served as a marker for a rowing regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat moored at a fixed point marks the start or turn of a course in rowing races.

clue.text: Covers centrally supported bands, £10 for admission

indicators.note: for admission means a piece is let inside another

parts.note: belts are bands
L is the pound sign, from libra, plus TEN

explanation.surface: Bands playing centrally charge ten pounds for entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centrally supported' belongs to the definition, describing how these covers stand.
explanation.definitionFit: These conical canvas shelters are held up by a single pole in the middle.

clue.text: As the Prince of Wales is to endless revels!

definitions.text: As the Prince of Wales is

indicators.note: revels means making merry wildly, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: The Prince of Wales is given to endless partying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revels' rearranges TO ENDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: The title Prince of Wales goes to the monarch's first-born male heir.

clue.text: Time to try on Kubrick's most prominent old hat

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court

indicators.note: the most prominent part of a word is taken as its front letter

explanation.surface: It is time to try on the most eye-catching of Stanley Kubrick's old hats.
explanation.walkthrough: The full phrase, minus its first two words, is OUT OF THE ARK, meaning very old-fashioned, like Noah's vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hopelessly antiquated is said to date from Noah's flood, the idiom opening with the dropped words.

clue.text: Hats off to everyone attending meal

indicators.note: hats are worn on top, so hats of words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Praise for everyone who comes along to a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the word names a light afternoon meal or an evening meal.

clue.text: Cumbrian flower old solver's snatched from the sky

indicators.note: snatched from means letters are taken away from the following words

parts.note: the letters left do also run on inside these two words, but that is a coincidence: the setter's device is taking out the old word for your
the solver is you, and the old form of your is thy

explanation.surface: An old flower of Cumbria that a solver has plucked out of the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: A flower is a river, something that flows; this one runs through Cumbria in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is something that flows, and this river runs in Cumbria.

clue.text: Endless depression with no warning

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the blues is a feeling of depression

explanation.surface: A bout of depression that never ends arrived without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: The full phrase is OUT OF THE BLUE, as from a clear sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening unexpectedly, like a bolt from a clear sky, is the idiom opening with the dropped words.

clue.text: Faulty coaches' terminus before getting parked outside Victoria

parts.note: terminus is the end, so the last letter of coaches

indicators.note: parked outside means placed round another piece

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A faulty coach finishes its route before parking outside London's Victoria coach station.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria Coach Station is London's main coach terminus. The full phrase is OUT OF SERVICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine or vehicle that is broken and unusable is said to be not working, the idiom opening with the dropped words.

clue.text: See 17
From OT, moves quickly north northeast, being into one of its authors

indicators.note: being into means a piece is placed in another

parts.note: Ruth is a book of the Old Testament, treated here as one of its writers

explanation.surface: From the Old Testament: someone moves quickly north-north-east, one of its writers.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is the Biblical form of runs, as in Psalm 23's 'my cup runneth over'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic third-person verb ending makes this the King James form of runs.

clue.text: Hawk keeping left, then right — skew-whiff!

indicators.note: keeping means holding one piece inside another

parts.note: a kite is a bird of prey, a kind of hawk

explanation.surface: A hawk veers left, then right, flying crookedly.
explanation.walkthrough: The full phrase is OUT OF KILTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Skew-whiff means askew or not straight; being off balance is the idiom opening with the dropped words.

clue.text: Loose shirt draped over a part-time fertility goddess?

indicators.note: draped over says one piece hangs round another
loose means the letters are let free and rearranged

explanation.surface: A baggy shirt is draped over a goddess of fertility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' rearranges SHIRT, which then wraps round A. She was a goddess of war as well as love and fertility, hence 'part-time'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Mesopotamian deity governed love and fertility among other domains.

clue.text: I cancel shifts, not keeping note of an American's personal space?

indicators.note: shifts means the letters change position
not keeping means one letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone cancels their work shifts, ignoring a note from an American about personal space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' rearranges I CANCEL and 'not keeping' drops N. This is the American spelling of coeliac, relating to the abdomen.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the abdomen, a person's own inner cavity, in US spelling.

clue.text: Prime Minister learner driver's preparing to drive around?

indicators.note: around means the outer piece goes round the inner one

parts.note: a golfer about to drive the ball is at the tee
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner driver is getting ready to set off around the block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' is a golfer: someone preparing to drive is AT TEE. L plates mark British learner drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee was the Labour prime minister of Britain from 1945 to 1951.

clue.text: For a change, he doesn't finally step in too far!

indicators.note: for a change signals that the letters are rearranged
finally picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Unusually, he doesn't step into deep water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a change' rearranges HE DOESNT with P. The full phrase is OUT OF ONE'S DEPTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in water too deep to stand, or beyond your ability, is the idiom that opens with the dropped words.

clue.text: High-calibre athletes (the majority leaving, winded) …

indicators.note: with most letters of the phrase gone, only a short run from within it remains

explanation.surface: Most top athletes have dropped out, exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: Most of the letters of 'High-calibre athletes' leave, and the run across 'calibre athletes' stays. The full phrase is OUT OF BREATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone panting after effort cannot breathe easily, the idiom opening with the dropped words.

clue.text: … dropped out of the competition — bizarre

definitions.meaning: a runner who quit a race has gone from the field of runners
strange and unexpected, the idiom being out of ..., from baseball

explanation.surface: Following on, the athletes quit the contest in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the entry itself; only the second, 'bizarre', is OUT OF LEFT FIELD, a baseball idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprise coming from an unexpected direction, as in baseball, is described by this idiom opening with the dropped words.

clue.text: One during first part of play briefly incapacitated

indicators.note: during means one piece sits within the time span of another
briefly means the phrase is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: act one is the opening section of a play
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone was injured during the opening act of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The full phrase is OUT OF ACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to take part through injury or breakdown is the idiom that opens with the dropped words.

clue.text: Atypical documentation of rights puts squeeze on American clubs

indicators.note: putting the squeeze on something presses round it, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a charter is a document granting rights
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: An unusual bill of rights pressures American nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: The full phrase is OUT OF CHARACTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour unlike someone's usual nature is the idiom that opens with the dropped words.
